title: Palo Alto Networks tracks more than 10 campaigns in which AI agents ran intrusions after web-shell access
date_note: Date of Unit 42's publication; the page gives no earlier day for the activity (campaigns July to September 2026).
sector: Government, logistics, hospitality, manufacturing, agriculture, education
geo_basis: researcher headquarters (Palo Alto Networks, Santa Clara, US)
summary: Palo Alto Networks' threat researchers say that between July and September 2026 they tracked more than 10 global campaigns in which AI agents carried out intrusions that began with a web shell on a vulnerable web application. In one case, they say the agent ran about 800 unique commands in 140 minutes of activity across two days. The report lists government, logistics, hospitality, manufacturing, agriculture and education among the targets.
plain: Palo Alto's threat researchers say they tracked more than 10 campaigns where AI agents did much of the hacking after attackers got a foothold through a vulnerable web application.
exec: Palo Alto Networks researchers report AI agents running intrusions across several sectors, so a vulnerable web application can be followed by fast, automated activity.
action: Palo Alto Networks' report advises GitLab operators to enforce multi-factor authentication, enable sign-in rate limiting, restrict access by IP where possible and keep instances up to date.
attack: web shell on vulnerable web application

evidence.quote: Between July and September 2026, we identified and tracked more than 10 global campaigns.
Throughout the attack, the AI agent executed about 800 unique commands at an inhuman pace.
the AI attacker was active for only 140 minutes across two days.

validation.note: Unit 42's own report (primary) and Cyber Press, which relays it.
